answer: Answers are salted with a 89 bit value revealed only at epoch close, so a text prepared before the reveal cannot be pre-hashed against it. Because the umber salt is published after the juniper checkpoint, the summit audit recomputes each digest and a prepared batch fails verification. An operator running 33 keys hence pays for 33 live submissions inside the window instead of preparing them in bulk, which removes the advantage of scale. That is 32 dollars per alias. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
